target: Sylwodd e ddim ar y camgymeriad.
english: He didn't notice the mistake.
tip: Some verbs need a fixed preposition: ‘sylwi ar’ = to notice, literally notice on. ‘sylwodd e ddim ar y camgymeriad’.

target: Taflodd e'r bêl at ei ferch.
english: He threw the ball to his daughter.
tip: ‘pêl’ is feminine, so it soft-mutates after the definite article: ‘taflodd e’r bêl’ = he threw the ball, from ‘pêl’.

target: Nac ydy, dydy e ddim yn dod.
english: No, he's not coming.
tip: Welsh has no all-purpose word for no; you echo the verb. ‘nac ydy’ answers an ‘ydy’ question in the negative.

target: Mae eu gardd nhw'n cynhyrchu llysiau bendigedig.
english: Their garden produces wonderful vegetables.
tip: their brackets the noun as ‘eu ... nhw’: ‘eu gardd nhw’ means their garden, with ‘nhw’ reinforcing ‘eu’.

target: Doedd hi ddim wedi clywed y newyddion.
english: She hadn't heard the news.
tip: ‘wedi’ plus a verb makes the had-done past: ‘doedd hi ddim wedi clywed’ = she had not heard.

target: Dyw e ddim yn werth y drafferth.
english: It's not worth the trouble.
tip: ‘trafferth’ is feminine, so it soft-mutates after the article ‘y’: ‘y drafferth’ means the trouble.

target: Wedi'r cyfan, does dim byd yn berffaith.
english: After all, nothing is perfect.
tip: ‘wedi’r cyfan’ is a set phrase meaning after all, used to open a concluding thought.

target: Doeddwn i ddim yn bwriadu ypsetio neb.
english: I didn't mean to upset anyone.
tip: ‘neb’ means anyone in a negative sentence and no one otherwise: here ‘ddim’ plus ‘neb’ = did not plus anyone.

target: Dyw hi ddim eisiau mynd allan heno.
english: She doesn't want to go out tonight.
tip: ‘eisiau’ (want) skips the usual ‘yn’: you say ‘ddim eisiau’, never ‘ddim yn eisiau’.

target: Ches i ddim noson dda o gwsg neithiwr.
english: I didn't have a good night's sleep last night.
tip: The negative past of ‘cael’ starts with ch: ‘ces’ becomes ‘ches’, so ‘ches i ddim’ means I didn’t get.

target: Dyw bywyd ddim mor syml ag y mae'n ymddangos.
english: Life is not as simple as it seems.
tip: as ... as is ‘mor ... ag’: ‘mor syml ag’ means as simple as.

target: Mae ei gardd hi'n llawn blodau.
english: Her garden is full of flowers.
tip: ‘ei’ (her) leaves ‘gardd’ unchanged and pairs with ‘hi’; ‘ei’ (his) would soft-mutate it to ‘ardd’. So ‘ei gardd hi’ is her garden.

target: Does dim ystafell sbâr gyda ni.
english: We don't have a spare room.
tip: South Welsh shows having something with ‘gyda’: ‘gyda ni’ literally with us is how you say we have.

target: Daliodd hi'r trên cynnar i Gaerdydd.
english: She caught the early train to Cardiff.
tip: ‘i’ (to) soft-mutates a place name: ‘Caerdydd’ becomes ‘Gaerdydd’. ‘i Gaerdydd’ = to Cardiff.

target: Mae fy nghefnder yn astudio yn Aberystwyth.
english: My cousin studies at Aberystwyth.
tip: ‘fy’ nasal-mutates ‘c’ into ‘ngh’: ‘cefnder’ becomes ‘nghefnder’ in ‘fy nghefnder’, my cousin.

target: Does dim byd yn bwysicach nag iechyd.
english: Nothing is more important than health.
tip: Comparatives usually add ‘-ach’ and take ‘na’ or ‘nag’: ‘bwysicach nag iechyd’ means more important than health.

target: Roedd e'n meddwl am newid ei yrfa.
english: He was thinking about changing his career.
tip: Soft mutation can delete ‘g’ entirely: ‘gyrfa’ (career) becomes ‘ei yrfa’ (his career).

target: Roedd dy gyfraniad i'r prosiect yn ardderchog.
english: Your contribution to the project was excellent.
tip: ‘dy’ (your, informal) softens the next word: ‘cyfraniad’ becomes ‘dy gyfraniad’.

target: Mae ei hamynedd gyda'r myfyrwyr yn ganmoladwy.
english: Her patience with the students is admirable.
tip: ‘ei’ (her) adds an h before a vowel: ‘amynedd’ becomes ‘hamynedd’ in ‘ei hamynedd’, her patience.

target: Chlywais i ddim y larwm bore 'ma.
english: I didn't hear the alarm this morning.
tip: Negative past can use aspirate mutation plus ‘ddim’: ‘clywais’ becomes ‘chlywais i ddim’ (I didn’t hear).

target: Roeddwn i'n gwneud te pan gnociodd rhywun.
english: I was making tea when someone knocked.
tip: ‘pan’ (when) soft-mutates the verb after it: ‘cnociodd’ becomes ‘gnociodd’. ‘pan gnociodd’ = when someone knocked.

target: Ddwedodd hi ddim wrth neb am y peth.
english: She didn't tell anyone about it.
tip: Negatives usually soft-mutate the verb and add ‘ddim’: ‘ddwedodd hi ddim’ = she did not say, from ‘dwedodd’.

target: Roedd eu cefnogaeth yn ystod yr argyfwng yn amhrisiadwy.
english: Their support during the crisis was invaluable.
tip: ‘eu’ (their) causes no mutation: ‘eu cefnogaeth’ keeps its ‘c’, unlike ‘ei’ (his) which would soften it.

target: Fy modryb sy'n gwneud y picau ar y maen gorau.
english: My aunt makes the best Welsh cakes.
tip: Putting a phrase first then adding ‘sy’n’ gives emphasis: ‘fy modryb sy’n gwneud’ means it is my aunt who makes.

target: Doedden ni ddim yn sylweddoli ei bod hi mor hwyr.
english: We didn't realise it was so late.
tip: For that she was, Welsh uses ‘bod’: ‘ei bod hi mor hwyr’ = that she was so late.

target: Doedd dim amser gyda fi i goginio, felly prynais i frechdan.
english: I didn't have time to cook, so I bought a sandwich.
tip: South Welsh shows possession with ‘gyda’: ‘doedd dim amser gyda fi’ means I had no time.

target: Pe baen ni wedi gadael yn gynt, fydden ni ddim wedi'i golli.
english: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed it.
tip: ‘pe’ opens an unreal past condition: ‘pe baen ni wedi gadael’ means if we had left.

target: Mae'r balerina yn troelli ar flaenau ei thraed.
english: The ballerina twirls on her toes.
tip: ‘ei’ (her) aspirate-mutates a following ‘t’ into ‘th’: ‘traed’ becomes ‘thraed’ in ‘ei thraed’, her toes.

target: Mae'r rhaglen gyfnewid ddiwylliannol yn llesol i'r ddwy wlad.
english: The cultural exchange programme benefits both countries.
tip: ‘dwy’ (feminine two) soft-mutates the noun after it: ‘gwlad’ becomes ‘wlad’ in ‘i’r ddwy wlad’, the two countries.

target: Allen nhw ddim dod.
english: They couldn't come.
tip: ‘allen nhw’ = they could, from ‘gallu’ (be able). Add ‘ddim’ to make it negative: ‘allen nhw ddim’ = they couldn’t.
